identity.description: GLM for zero-inflated CONTINUOUS targets: with variance power p in (1,2) the Tweedie family is a compound Poisson-gamma — an exact point mass at zero plus a right-skewed positive tail — modeled in ONE equation. The canonical shape of insurance pure premium, per-member revenue, and claim/donation totals.

consumes.note: non-negative continuous target with (typically) a spike at exactly zero; exposure passthrough supported

emits.note: the expected value (e.g. pure premium) that already integrates zero-probability and positive-severity; the fitted compound distribution is defined, though its density is evaluated by series approximation
log-link multiplicative effects on the expected total — the rating-factor story insurance actuaries read directly

var_power.note: the Tweedie p in variance = phi*mu^p; p in (1,2) is compound Poisson-gamma (exact zeros + continuous tail); p->1 approaches Poisson, p->2 approaches gamma

eql.note: extended quasi-likelihood for loglike-based diagnostics; the true Tweedie density has no closed form

invariances.why: unpenalized IRLS is scale-equivariant, but the searchable elastic-net penalty is unit-dependent and ill-scaled columns condition the working weighted least squares badly
log-linear mean structure — a monotone transform of a covariate changes the fitted mean function
IRLS has no missing-value mechanism; rows must be complete

assumes the conditional distribution is Tweedie with variance = phi*mu^p — for p in (1,2) a compound Poisson-gamma whose point mass at zero and right-skewed positive branch must actually match the data's zero-spike-plus-tail shape
p+1 mean parameters fit fine at modest n, but var_power selection needs enough rows to resolve the mean-variance power law across the mean's range
log-linear mean extends beyond the covariate range with exponential growth

featureStats.why: Tweedie's raison d'etre — a material point mass at EXACTLY zero atop a continuous positive tail is the compound Poisson-gamma signature; near-zero fraction gates to gamma/lognormal, extreme fraction gates to an explicit two-part model
the positive branch is gamma-shaped (right-skewed); a symmetric positive target suggests the Tweedie variance law is the wrong power family
regressing log group-variance on log group-mean estimates the power p directly from data — the slope IS the var_power the fit assumes, checked before it is trusted

modelMetrics.why: the family-native goodness-of-fit at the chosen p; comparing deviance across candidate var_power values is the standard p-selection scan
the estimated dispersion in variance = phi*mu^p; a phi far from stable across subgroups says the single power law is misspecified

edgeCases.behavior: Tweedie support is [0, inf) for p in (1,2) — likelihood undefined
the zero-mass component is vestigial; p drifts toward 2
edgeCases.note: a gamma GLM (p=2) is the simpler honest model

edgeCases.behavior: p in (0,1) is not a valid Tweedie family; p=1/p=2 change the support semantics
mean estimate dominated by the zero mass; positive-branch coefficients starved
edgeCases.note: explicit two-part (frequency x severity) or zero_inflated modeling

driver.constructor: sm.GLM(y, sm.add_constant(X), family=sm.families.Tweedie(var_power=..., link=..., eql=True), exposure=...).fit() or .fit_regularized(alpha=..., L1_wt=...)
driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: add_constant; predict returns the expected value; wrapper scans var_power over a small grid by deviance when not user-fixed
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded IRLS fit; predict is thread-safe

placementClaims.why: no native NaN handling; dropped rows bias both zero-frequency and severity components
log/Yeo-Johnson of skewed covariates improves the log-linear mean fit; the TARGET must stay untransformed — the zero mass is the signal, not noise
scale-equivariant unpenalized, but standardization conditions IRLS and is needed under the elastic-net penalty
categorical rating factors must be design-encoded before fitting
